The story so far: On Sunday (October 11, 2026) the election campaign of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva accused the tech giant, Meta (parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram) of deliberately restricting and blocking social media content of the leader on its various platforms, particularly Instagram.

It further states that post the first round of voting, which took place on October 4 wherein Mr. Bolsonaro came out on top, Mr. Lula’s and other left leaders’ profiles “suddenly disappeared from Instagram’s search function.”

The statement added that, “the series of technical issues... raises strong suspicions that Meta’s actions constitute an attempt to interfere in the Brazilian electoral process to the benefit of Flavio Bolsonaro’s candidacy”.

Meta’s Brazil office denied the charges, calling them “simply false” and “not supported by the facts.” The company said that it was committed to ensuring a level-playing field during elections, and that such glitches were global and not just localised in Brazil with the intention to tamper anyone’s candidacy.

This is not the first time where Meta, formerly Facebook, has been accused of election interference. The most infamous example of the same was the Cambridge Analytica scandal in the U.S. which dealt with the 2016 presidential campaign between Republican candidate Donald Trump and Democrat Hillary Clinton.

Premium headphones have evolved from being primarily about sound to becoming an everyday device that needs to get several things right. Comfort, ANC, call quality, battery life and how well they fit into an active lifestyle now matter just as much. That is also why the premium headphones space has become increasingly competitive, with brands finding different ways to make their products stand out.

The Beats 360 enters this space at ₹42,900, bringing interchangeable earcup and headband cushions, IPX4 resistance and a design aimed at both workouts and everyday use. These additions give the Beats 360 a distinct identity, but the bigger question is how well that approach works in daily use. So, let’s find out if the Beats 360 has what it takes to stand out.

The biggest change with the Beats 360 is its approach to design. Beats has made the earcups and headband cushions removable, which gives you more flexibility than most premium headphones. You get Performance Knit cushions for workouts and UltraPlush cushions for everyday listening.

I particularly like this idea because it makes sense beyond just customisation. The Performance Knit material is better suited to an active session, while the softer UltraPlush option makes more sense when you are working or travelling. It gives the Beats 360 two personalities without changing the headphones themselves.

The IPX4 rating also adds some much-needed practicality. Sweat and water resistance is still uncommon among premium over-ear headphones. That gives the Beats 360 an advantage if you plan to use them during workouts.
